newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian phone workers threaten hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian phone workers threaten hunger strike.

text.p: Indian telecommunications workers threatened to go on hunger strike as a work stoppage by more than one million government employees entered its third day on Friday.
A group of trade unions representing government telecommunications workers said in a statement late on Thursday they planned to start an indefinite hunger strike in the Indian capital on Saturday.
The hunger strike would be extended to state headquarters on Monday if the dispute over a wage row was not settled.

Striking telecommunications, postal and income tax workers employed by the government demand the elimination of a ceiling on annual bonus payments, arguing that a cap on bonuses for railway workers had already been lifted.
The strike has crippled government mail services.
Some 15 million letters had piled up in the general post office in the nation's financial capital Bombay, the Press Trust of India said.
The strike was a windfall for private courier services, which said they were flooded with requests.
Telecommunications services, which are largely automated, have fared better. But operator-related services and repair and maintenance were badly disrupted.

In a sign that the strike was spreading, supervisors in the Department of Post and Telecommunications announced they would join the work stoppage on Friday. The supervisors' union claimed it had 100,000 workers across the country.
Earlier the two main communist parties came out in support of the unions' demands, putting extra pressure on Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The two communist parties provide crucial backing for Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition government.
On Thursday, Communications Minister Beni Prasad Varma said he sympathised with the strikers and would present their case to the government.
But Deve Gowda was in the remote northeast of India on a week-long trip, all but ruling out a cabinet meeting on the matter until he returns next week, officials said.
The Hindu newspaper said Varma spoke to Deve Gowda on Thursday evening. It quoted sources close to the communications minister as saying "all signs point to a rapprochement".
Union leaders were also reported to be heartened by a statement by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, who was travelling in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
Chidambaram urged the government workers to call off their strike and wait until Deve Gowda's cabinet could meet to take a decision on their demands.
The finance minister said the cabinet had looked favourably on the demand by railway workers for the elimination of the ceiling on bonus payments.
"If a similar proposal comes from the Communications Ministry, the cabinet will certainly consider it and take a decision," United News of India quoted Chidambaram as saying.
